title: Iowa band spells ‘DEREK’ at halftime to honor member who died after collapse
content:
IOWA CITY, Iowa — The Iowa Hawkeye Marching Band spelled out “DEREK” at the end of its halftime performance in commemoration of former bandmate Derek Phillips, who died Tuesday after suffering a heart attack during the stifling heat at Kinnick Stadium last week.

In a performance Phillips helped create but was postponed by one week, the Hawkeye Marching Band performed “50 Years of the Muppet Show” during halftime. During the final song — Rainbow Connection — the band shifted into formation to spell Derek’s name. The sold-out crowd at Kinnick Stadium gave the band a standing ovation.

Phillips, 20, collapsed during Iowa’s season opener on Sept. 5 when the air temperature soared to 93 degrees, and the heat index reached at least 105 degrees. Family took Phillips off life support Monday.

Iowa conducted a moment of silence for Phillips before the National Anthem. Phillips led the Hawkeye Marching Band’s mellophone section and was a multi-year member.

The Hawkeye Marching Band students and staff will wear a black pin on their jackets and shirts this season. Dozens of other bands have offered their tributes to Phillips, including Iowa State’s Cyclone Marching Band, which will wear a black-and-gold pin with an outline of the state of Iowa and the letters “DIFD” (Do It For Derek) on their collars for the remainder of the season.

On Saturday, Western Michigan’s Bronco Marching Band dedicated its performance of “Amazing Grace” following Saturday’s game to Phillips’ memory. Nebraska’s Cornhusker Marching Band wore gold ribbons to honor Phillips during its game against Bowling Green.
